You read transcripts of Bitcoin videos. For each EXCERPT below, the sentences inside <selected> are a clip
that may be shown on its own. Use the whole excerpt (what comes before and after) to judge the selected words. You do
not know how the clip will be used.

<excerpt label="M" channel="Bitcoin Mechanic" video_title="The State Of Payments In "Bitcoin"" published="2026-11-04T22:36" show_date="2026-11-12">So when I lost it, I went to buy it again, right? And at the time, they accepted Bitcoin as payment. and I went to pay for it, and I don't remember exactly what it did, but I couldn't get it to give me a Bitcoin address. It gave me like use Binance wallet or Coinbase wallet or Metamask, and each of these required me to set up some sort of K -Y -C account with some fucking company that will only open a link to the relevant application that I would have to have installed and be signed in with my identity connected to it. It would not give me a Bitcoin address to pay with. because it doesn't actually respect the underlying neutrality of the protocol. Where have you ever heard a Bitcoin complain about that? Twitter is our town square. That is where most of the majority around what happens on Bitcoin occurs in the world. It happens on Twitter. I'm not saying there aren't hundreds of other venues for it, but I'm pretty sure that is the most important one. It accepts Bitcoin, except it doesn't... allow us to actually pay each other in a peer -to -peer way. It requires permission. It's done it in a way that undermines the entire point of it, the peer -to -peer payment network aspect of it, the fact that I can pay any address, as long as there's a valid address, I can pay it, and I can pay it from any valid UTXO. That is undermined by enforcing a system on top of it that says, no, we need your identity to be attached to your activity somehow. <selected>It becomes completely pointless.</selected> There is no difference between making payments that way and making payments with a credit card. It's the same system. You haven't escaped Fiat at all. All you've done is escape inflation by being involved in Bitcoin at that point. You haven't... freed yourself from the tyranny of regulated payment networks, which was one of the main points. There are two points to Bitcoin. There's a disinflationary currency that allows you to store value and not lose it and store your work and labor over long periods of time. That's half of it. The other half of it is I can make payments to anyone, anywhere, and no one can stop me. That's the other half of it. And the Bip -110ers and the XBT heads and all those, we have spoken about how the second aspect can be undermined with centralized mining and top -down soft forks and things like that. And I really want to stress that all of that can be true, but this is already gone. It's already a thing that's not there anymore. It's not just X premium.</excerpt>

For each excerpt answer:
- "speaker_changes_inside": does the speaker change inside the selected words? "yes" / "no" / "uncertain"
- "view": whose view the selected words express: "own_sincere" (the speaker's own sincere assertion), "attributed"
  (someone else's view, quoted or reported), "hypothetical", "conditional" (true only under a condition), "sarcastic",
  "question", "reading_aloud" (reading a post or article), "ad_read", "joke", or "uncertain"
- "referents": every pronoun or pointing word in the selected words (it, they, this, that, he, she, today, here...)
  that points at something specific, with what it refers to; "inside": true if the selected words themselves give
  its antecedent or the predicate that completes it (an ellipsis completed by an earlier selected sentence: "It's not
  Bitcoin that's getting hacked. It's other intermediaries." = other intermediaries are getting hacked), or it points
  only at a general topic the clip presupposes; "inside": false if a listener needs the words before or after the
  selection; "changes_assertion": "yes" if resolving it differently would change WHAT THE SPEAKER ASSERTS, "no" if
  not, "uncertain". Leave out words that point at nothing outside: a dummy "it" ("it's raining", "it's not X that
  ...", where X is in the selection), and a generic "we" / "you" / "they" meaning people in general
- "conditions": any condition or time frame that governs the selected words, and whether it is INSIDE them
- "retraction": "none", or what the speaker later in the excerpt retracts or qualifies about the selected words
- "time_ok": "yes" if every time word in the selected words (today, now, this week, just, recently, a "current"
  price) still holds on the show date given when the video was published (both on the excerpt), or there is none;
  "no" if it is stale; "uncertain"
- "proposition": in one sentence, what the speaker asserts in the selected words, read in context
- "certainty": "certain", "likely", "possible", "speculative" or "uncertain"
- "speaker_is": "host" if the excerpt shows that the speaker of the selected words is the channel's own host,
  "guest" if it shows a guest or another person speaking them, "uncertain" otherwise; "speaker_evidence": the exact
  words of the excerpt that show it (copied exactly, e.g. the host's own "welcome back to my channel"), or ""
